summary: 120-foot steel tower moved in 1972 from the August A. Busch site to Gutherie, Callaway County, MO; set on fire in 1974; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Dismantled at the August A. Busch site and re-erected at Gutherie in 1972; no source read says whether it still stands there

events.note: Dismantled near St. Charles and re-erected just south of Gutherie on Callaway County Route J; replaced the wooden Reform tower
Eugene McCormack, former Reform towerman, assigned to the Gutherie tower
Special landscape grading completed at the Gutherie tower site in fiscal 1973-74
Set on fire on July 1, 1974; an 18-year-old from Fulton later entered a guilty plea to arson of state property
Cab replaced, per the fiscal 1974-75 annual report

corrections.why: The 1972 sources describe the tower being dismantled at the August A. Busch site and re-erected at Gutherie, so 'gone' fits the original site rather than Gutherie. No cited source says whether the tower still stands at Gutherie, so the record's 'gone' may be right for the present but is not supported by these sources.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The sources use three names for the agency: Missouri Conservation Commission (page heading), Missouri Department of Conservation (annual report) and Missouri Conservation Department (1974 article). These appear to be one agency under names that changed over time.

notes_for_editor: The three Forest Lookouts pages reproduce 1972-1975 newspaper items and Missouri annual reports; the originals were not read. Build date of the August A. Busch tower, its removal date and any post-1975 history were not found, so the story leaves them out. The record's status 'gone' has no page-level support: the Gutherie page has no 'Removed' line (unlike Higdon and Highway 60), and the central-lookouts source record carries status_raw 'dismantled', which matches the 1972 move from the Busch site. A Missouri Conservation History Facebook post, seen only as a search snippet (page not readable), describes the tower as originally near St. Louis in the August Busch Memorial Conservation Area; the 1972 newspaper says near St. Charles. Not reconciled and not cited. The August A. Busch site may deserve its own record. No photos found in this pass. Budget used: 2 searches, 3 page reads. Fact-check 2026-10-21: story wording tightened where it copied quotes, one missing footnote added, dates and the prosecutor's name added to evidence.
